failure_reason: Direct HTTP (curl_cffi) and headless Playwright were blocked by Akamai on every /shop/ path; headed Playwright (real Chrome, non-headless) reached several pages then also hit a 403. Escalated to Claude-in-Chrome (last-resort tier; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow) which is a browser instance shared across 10 concurrent workers on this task -- partway through verification its tab-group/session assignment became unstable (rapid, uncontrollable reassignment to different tab groups between consecutive tool calls), which stopped further page reads. 6 of 8 known Clearance sub-listings were fully verified with exact counts before this happened; the remaining 2 (Rugs Clearance, Bath & Beach Clearance) were confirmed to exist and load (page title verified) but their exact item counts could not be captured before the tooling became unusable for this pass.
notes: Access route as above. Navigation discovery: the homepage header nav has a 'Sale' link (/shop/sale/) but NO direct Clearance link in the header; the genuine Clearance taxonomy was found via the site's own shop-sitemap-index.xml (fetched directly via curl_cffi, 611 URLs), which lists a distinct family of '/shop/sale/*-clearance/' URLs (backpacks-clearance, furniture1-clearance, bedding-clearance, decor-accessories-clearance, window-treatments-clearance, rug-clearance, bath-beach-clearance) separate from the much larger family of generic '/shop/sale/*-sale/' URLs (bedroom-furniture-sale, bedding-sale, rugs-sale, christmas-sale, black-friday-deals-20, cyber-monday-deals-20, seasonal-sale, etc.) plus a top-level 'clearance-all/' URL. Opening clearance-all/ confirmed the site's OWN breadcrumb taxonomy is 'Sale > Clearance > Shop All Clearance' -- i.e. the site itself nests a distinct 'Clearance' node one level under the generic 'Sale' node, and its own pricing-label config (seen in the homepage's embedded JSON state) defines 'clearance' and 'sale' as two separate price-badge labels. On the clearance-all/ listing, individual product badges read 'CLEARANCE' (not 'SALE') confirming this is the site's genuine permanent-markdown merchandising concept, matching the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale test. The generic '*-sale/' pages (bedroom-furniture-sale, bedding-sale, seasonal-sale, black-friday-deals-20, etc.) were deliberately excluded as generic temporary promotional Sale pages, not Clearance, per the brief -- none carried a clearance/outlet/final-clearance/last-chance signal in their own naming or breadcrumb. Each verified Clearance sub-listing showed the same 'Sale > Clearance > <Dept> Clearance' breadcrumb and an exact '<N> Items' count on the page (not a facet-URL redirect like the Best Sellers department pages), so these are clean, unambiguous per-department Clearance PLPs, not filter permutations.
